data.narrative:
Helical Fusion is a Series B nuclear energy company founded by Takaya Taguchi and Junichi Miyazawa, having raised $98M to date. The valuation assessment draws on a comparison universe of 11 peers across the nuclear energy sector—3 public companies (OKLO, NNE, SMR) and 8 private entities including Valar Atomics, Helion, Oklo, X-Energy, and Nano Nuclear Energy.

The stage-progression method was the applicable triangulation approach. Using total capital raised of $98M as a proxy baseline valuation and applying a typical Series B-to-later-stage step-up multiplier of 1.9x yields an implied valuation of $186M. The peer-median approach was not applicable due to insufficient depth in same-stage and adjacent-stage comparables within the nuclear energy sector; while six same-sector peers exist in the dataset, fewer than three datapoints met the narrow filters required for reliable median derivation, making an all-sector fallback methodologically unsuitable.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $158M to $214M, centered on $186M. This single-method result introduces material uncertainty around the point estimate. Key sensitivities include the appropriateness of the 1.9x step-up multiplier to Helical Fusion's specific capital efficiency and competitive position, the degree to which public nuclear comps reflect private-market dynamics, and the stage definition of prospective Series C or later financing. Additional peer density in the narrow-stage nuclear cohort would strengthen conviction in this range.
